name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt the 3px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px inner #fff at 80% opacity. This balances visibility for keyboard users with reduced distraction, especially on high-contrast screens. The thicker ring ensures touch targets remain clear on mobile, while the semi-transparent inner cutout softens the harshness that full opacity can create. Trade-off: the 80% opacity may be slightly less visible in bright sunlight, but the 3px width compensates by increasing the ring’s presence.

name: Reader
text: The 3px ring risks blurring into adjacent interactive elements on high-contrast backgrounds, making it harder to distinguish focus. A 2px ring with 3:1 contrast against the background meets WCAG 2.2 but may fail on light surfaces. Test both on a 100% white background with adjacent buttons—if the ring disappears, revert to a 2px #005fcc ring with a 1px #fff border.

name: Ramp
text:
We should adopt the 2px solid #005fcc focus ring, as it meets the WCAG 2.2 contrast requirement and minimizes blurring into adjacent elements on high-contrast backgrounds. This decision trades off some touch target clarity on mobile for better focus distinction on desktop screens. By accepting this trade-off, we prioritize keyboard users who need a clear focus indicator, while still maintaining some visibility for touch users. The 2px ring is a better compromise than the original 3px proposal, as it reduces visual noise and improves overall usability.

name: Reader
text: The 2px ring fails on light surfaces where 3:1 contrast isn’t enough—adjacent buttons disappear into the focus ring. Test a 3px ring with 4.5:1 contrast against both white and dark backgrounds; if it blurs, add a 1px inner white cutout at 50% opacity. Settle with a live contrast checker and user testing on both mobile and desktop.
